clue.text: Crafts based on fundamental duplicity

parts.note: a twin-hulled boat is literally double at its base, so 'fundamental duplicity' is doubleness at the bottom rather than deceit

explanation.surface: Sounds like a sneer at schemes or trades built on basic dishonesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crafts' means boats, not skills or wiles, and 'duplicity' is taken literally as twoness: these vessels have two hulls underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: These sailing boats have two parallel hulls, so their foundation is literally doubled.

clue.text: Dunce's cap is, maybe, the case for a dreamer

definitions.note: loose: the definition names the person, the answer is the dreamer's habit of retreating into fantasy

indicators.note: the clue words form a case or casing around the answer, which sits inside 'Dunce's cap is, maybe'

explanation.surface: Suggests a dunce's cap might be the right headgear for a daydreamer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the case for' looks like 'the argument for', but the words before it literally encase the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Retreating into fantasy away from reality is what characterises a daydreamer.

clue.text: Fat, it is said, of the land

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the word for fat matches the name of the country

parts.note: grease is animal fat

explanation.surface: Sounds like a biblical 'fat of the land' phrase about plenty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The fat of the land' is a stock phrase for abundance, which hides that 'the land' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A country is a land, here the Mediterranean nation home of Athens.

clue.text: We are cut down or used to be

definitions.meaning: 'we are' shortened to the contraction with an apostrophe, which dropped gives these letters
the plural past tense of the verb to be

explanation.surface: A rueful lament from people diminished from what they once were.
explanation.walkthrough: The contraction for 'we are' loses its apostrophe in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of 'be' describes what someone or something formerly was.

clue.text: Get NHS rent reviewed and grow stronger

indicators.note: something reviewed is gone over and reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A call for the National Health Service to have its rent reassessed and so become more robust.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow stronger is to gain in power or firmness, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Mould bird in metal? No way!

parts.note: to forge metal is to shape or mould it
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: Someone scorns the idea of casting a bird figure in metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in metal' completes the picture of forging, which works metal; it gives no letters of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dismissive refusals telling someone the idea is out of the question.

clue.text: And, what is more, a real gent!

parts.note: a swell is an old word for a fashionable gentleman

explanation.surface: An exclamation of admiration added on: and he is a true gentleman too!
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean 'also' or 'in addition'.

clue.text: He races in circles

definitions.note: a man, here a male first name

indicators.note: a word that runs round in a circle reads the same either way, so the name is the same backwards as forwards

parts.note: a man, here a male first name

explanation.surface: Describes a driver or runner going round a circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'He', a man's name; the rest says the name goes round and comes back to itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A German male first name, so it can stand for a man, 'He'.

clue.text: Sailor told to go round globe, taking things in?

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a standard abbreviation for a sailor

indicators.note: one piece is said to go round the other, so it encloses it

parts.note: sent means told to go, as in sent away
an orb is a globe

explanation.surface: A sailor instructed to circumnavigate the world, perhaps drinking in the sights.
explanation.definitionFit: Something soaking up liquid, or a mind soaking up knowledge, takes things in.

clue.text: Start working as a film actor

definitions.meaning: a film actor at work is on the studio set, read as two words

explanation.surface: Someone begins a job acting in movies.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean the beginning of something; split in two it is where film actors work.

clue.text: Made out in expert world of scholars

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the word for expert

parts.note: an ace is an expert

indicators.note: the word made is put out of its order, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is spotted in a specialist realm of academics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like 'made out' as in discerned, but it is the anagram signal; 'expert' is the container, a crossword staple meaning a champion.
explanation.definitionFit: The academic community, the realm of universities and learning.

clue.text: Attic studio ideal for this artist?

definitions.text: Attic studio ideal for this artist?

parts.words: Attic studio ideal for this artist?
parts.note: Attic with a capital means Athenian or Greek, so a Greek-style studio suits the painter whose nickname means 'the Greek'

explanation.surface: Suggests a garret workshop would suit a particular painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attic' is not a loft but the adjective for Attica, the region of Athens; the painter, born in Crete, was called 'the Greek' in Spanish.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cretan-born Spanish Renaissance painter Domenikos Theotokopoulos, known by this nickname.

clue.text: Quick drink about teatime?

definitions.note: in the old sense of living, as in 'the quick and the dead'

indicators.note: the drink goes about, around, the time

parts.note: ale is beer
four o'clock, IV in Roman numerals, is the traditional British hour for afternoon tea

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a swift beverage around afternoon tea time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' looks like it describes the drink, but it is the definition in its old sense of living.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick in its archaic sense means living, as in 'the quick and the dead'.

clue.text: Dive for weapon used after dark

indicators.note: the weapon is used after dark, so it comes after in the answer

parts.note: night is the dark time
a club is a bludgeon

explanation.surface: Seems to ask what weapon someone grabs for at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dive' is the noun for a seedy bar or venue, not a plunge.
explanation.definitionFit: A dive is slang for a disreputable late-night drinking or dancing venue.

clue.text: One is distracted with northern stars, they're very bright

indicators.note: a distracted mind is jumbled, so the letters of one are scrambled

parts.note: stars are lights in the sky

explanation.surface: A person is dazzled by stars in the northern sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is distracted' rearranges ONE to NEO.
explanation.definitionFit: Glowing gas-filled signs and tubes are famously bright and garish.

clue.text: Late, it turns in after me

indicators.note: the turned word goes inside the phrase for after me

parts.note: coming after me means behind me

indicators.note: the word it turns round, reading backwards

explanation.surface: Someone notes a person arriving tardily after them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it turns' reads as a story of someone turning in after you, but it is a reversal signal; 'after me' must be read as a positional phrase to give the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Running behind schedule means arriving late.

clue.text: Well protected, gumshield and all?

parts.note: a boxer's mouth guard literally arms the teeth, a playful take on the idiom for being fully equipped

explanation.surface: Describes a boxer or rugby player kitted out with every piece of protection.
explanation.walkthrough: A gumshield is a mouth guard worn in contact sports.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being heavily equipped with weapons, taken here as protection for the mouth.

clue.text: Get less iron

definitions.meaning: to iron clothes is to remove creases

explanation.definitionFit: To diminish is to get less; split as de-crease, it means remove wrinkles by pressing.

clue.text: In income distribution, company is thrifty

indicators.note: the company abbreviation goes in the rearranged letters
distribution spreads things around, so the letters of income are rearranged

explanation.surface: A firm careful with how it shares out its earnings is frugal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distribution' looks like sharing out money but signals the anagram; the company abbreviation sits in the anagram's second and third places.
explanation.definitionFit: Economic can mean sparing or careful with money, a near-synonym of frugal.

clue.text: Half an organ stop?

parts.note: semi means half
the colon is an organ of the body, the large intestine

explanation.surface: Suggests pulling out part of a church organ's stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ stop' looks like a musical stop, but the organ is bodily and the stop is a punctuation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: This punctuation mark is a stop, a pause stronger than a comma.

clue.text: More like those blessed with a worldly inheritance?

definitions.text: More like those blessed with a worldly inheritance?

parts.words: More like those blessed with a worldly inheritance?
parts.note: refers to the Beatitude 'Blessed are the ... for they shall inherit the earth', describing the gentle

explanation.surface: Asks who is more like the heirs to a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sermon on the Mount says the humble and gentle shall inherit the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of a word meaning humble and gentle, as in the Beatitude.

clue.text: Fruit suggests trouble afoot

definitions.meaning: the nut of the oak tree is its fruit
a corn is a painful patch on the foot, so a corn is trouble on the foot

explanation.surface: Something gives warning that mischief is brewing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afoot' normally means brewing, but here it means literally on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The oak's nut is botanically its fruit.

clue.text: Come round to a strangely weak point

indicators.note: something done strangely is out of its usual order, so weak is rearranged

parts.note: N, north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone regains consciousness at an oddly feeble moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges WEAK to WAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: To come round after fainting is to wake up.

clue.text: Drifter of a coldly detached nature

definitions.text: Drifter of a coldly detached nature

parts.words: Drifter of a coldly detached nature
parts.note: a wanderer with a frosty manner, read literally as a frozen mass drifting after breaking from a glacier

explanation.surface: Describes an aloof, unfeeling vagrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coldly detached' is literally true: the mass is frozen and has broken off a glacier or ice shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: A floating mass of frozen water that has broken off and drifts in the sea.

clue.text: I get an encore — or the bird

parts.note: bis, Latin for twice, is a call for an encore

explanation.surface: A performer either gets an encore or is booed off, getting the bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting the bird' is British for being booed or hissed, which steers away from the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-legged wading bird with a curved bill, sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Confirm a wild animal has escaped

parts.note: a bear is a wild animal
an escaped animal is out

explanation.surface: A report verifies that a dangerous creature is on the loose.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear out a claim is to support or corroborate it.

clue.text: Steal up around a wild beast

indicators.note: the reversed word goes around the letter A
in a down clue, up reads the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to rob is to steal

explanation.surface: Someone creeps up on a dangerous animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ROB into BOR, which goes around A.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild pig, the male of which is a fierce beast.

clue.text: One can't imagine being without them

definitions.text: One can't imagine being without them

parts.words: One can't imagine being without them
parts.note: read literally: to imagine at all, you need mental notions or concepts

explanation.surface: Sounds like someone who cannot picture life without loved ones or comforts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can't imagine being without' is usually fond devotion, but here it is literal: imagining needs these.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoughts or concepts are what imagination is made of.

clue.text: Figure offered by corporation accepting a prize novel

indicators.note: the stomach word accepts, takes inside, the rearranged letters

parts.note: corporation is old humorous slang for a paunch, a tum

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of a prize are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A company accepts an award for a work of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' looks like a company, but it is old British slang for a pot belly; 'novel' looks like a book but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-sided geometric shape, a type of quadrilateral, is a figure.
